languages.name: Elixir
languages.description: BEAM/OTP language reference focused on concurrency, supervision, observability, polling, and resilient WynCommand/WynOS-style services.

categories.name: Core Language
categories.description: Immutable data, functions, pattern matching, and pipelines.

entries.title: Pattern matching
entries.summary: Match and destructure values with = and function heads.
entries.definition: Match and destructure values with = and function heads.
entries.mental_model: The left side is a shape the right side must fit.

entries.title: Immutable data
entries.summary: Values are not mutated in place; transformations produce new values.
entries.definition: Values are not mutated in place; transformations produce new values.
entries.mental_model: Think persistent snapshots rather than mutable containers.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Shows old and new lists coexist.

entries.title: Anonymous functions
entries.summary: Create function values with fn ... end.
entries.definition: Create function values with fn ... end.
entries.mental_model: Behavior can be stored and passed like data.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
double = fn x -> x * 2 end
IO.puts(double.(21))

entries.title: Named functions and guards
entries.summary: Define multi-clause functions that dispatch by pattern and guard.
entries.signature: def f(pattern) when guard do ... end
entries.definition: Define multi-clause functions that dispatch by pattern and guard.
entries.mental_model: Function clauses form a top-to-bottom pattern decision table.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
defmodule Classifier do
  def sign(x) when x > 0, do: :positive
  def sign(_), do: :other
end

entries.title: Pipe operator
entries.summary: Pass the previous expression as the first argument of the next call.
entries.definition: Pass the previous expression as the first argument of the next call.
entries.mental_model: Data flows left to right through transformations.

entries.title: with
entries.summary: Chain pattern-matched success steps and short-circuit on failure.
entries.definition: Chain pattern-matched success steps and short-circuit on failure.
entries.mental_model: A happy-path pipeline for tagged results.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
with {:ok, a} <- {:ok, 20},
     {:ok, b} <- {:ok, 22} do
  a + b
end

entries.title: spawn/1
entries.summary: Create a lightweight BEAM process running a function.
entries.definition: Create a lightweight BEAM process running a function.
entries.mental_model: Processes are isolated actors with independent heaps and mailboxes.

entries.title: send/2
entries.summary: Send an immutable message to another process mailbox.
entries.definition: Send an immutable message to another process mailbox.
entries.mental_model: Messages are asynchronous envelopes placed in a mailbox.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Sends a tagged tuple back to the parent.

entries.title: receive
entries.summary: Pattern-match messages from the current process mailbox.
entries.definition: Pattern-match messages from the current process mailbox.
entries.mental_model: Mailbox scanning plus pattern matching.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
send(self(), {:status, :ok})
receive do
  {:status, value} -> IO.inspect(value)
end

entries.title: Process.monitor/1
entries.summary: Observe another process and receive a message if it terminates.
entries.definition: Observe another process and receive a message if it terminates.
entries.mental_model: Monitoring is one-way observation without linking failure fate.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
pid = spawn(fn -> :ok end)
ref = Process.monitor(pid)
receive do
  {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, reason} -> IO.inspect(reason)
end

entries.title: Links
entries.summary: Couple process lifecycles so failures can propagate according to trap-exit behavior.
entries.definition: Couple process lifecycles so failures can propagate according to trap-exit behavior.
entries.mental_model: Links form failure-propagation relationships used by OTP supervision.

categories.name: OTP Building Blocks
categories.description: Higher-level concurrency patterns for resilient systems.

entries.title: Task
entries.summary: Run one-off concurrent work with structured APIs.
entries.definition: Run one-off concurrent work with structured APIs.
entries.mental_model: A Task wraps a process around a single unit of work.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Runs work concurrently and waits for 42.

entries.title: Agent
entries.summary: Manage simple shared state behind a process API.
entries.definition: Manage simple shared state behind a process API.
entries.mental_model: State lives in one process; callers interact through serialized requests.

entries.title: GenServer
entries.summary: Implement long-lived stateful processes with standardized call/cast/info callbacks.
entries.definition: Implement long-lived stateful processes with standardized call/cast/info callbacks.
entries.mental_model: GenServer is a disciplined mailbox loop with conventions.

examples.title: Example

entries.title: Supervisor
entries.summary: Start and restart child processes according to a supervision strategy.
entries.definition: Start and restart child processes according to a supervision strategy.
entries.mental_model: Let processes crash, then use supervisors as recovery machinery.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
children = [{Task, fn -> Process.sleep(:infinity) end}]
Supervisor.start_link(children, strategy: :one_for_one)
examples.explanation: Starts a supervisor with one child.

entries.title: Registry
entries.summary: Associate names/keys with processes for dynamic lookup and dispatch.
entries.definition: Associate names/keys with processes for dynamic lookup and dispatch.
entries.mental_model: A process directory maintained inside the BEAM.

entries.title: Mix
entries.summary: Use Elixir's build tool for projects, dependencies, tasks, and releases.
entries.signature: mix new / mix run / mix test
entries.definition: Use Elixir's build tool for projects, dependencies, tasks, and releases.
entries.mental_model: Mix is the project/build command surface for Elixir.

entries.title: Logger
entries.summary: Emit structured runtime log messages.
entries.definition: Emit structured runtime log messages.
entries.mental_model: Centralized process-friendly logging.

entries.title: Process.info/2
entries.summary: Inspect process metadata such as message queue length or memory.
entries.definition: Inspect process metadata such as message queue length or memory.
entries.mental_model: Ask the BEAM runtime about a process without opening its internals.

entries.title: :timer.send_interval/2
entries.summary: Schedule recurring messages to the current process.
entries.definition: Schedule recurring messages to the current process.
entries.mental_model: Turn time into mailbox events, ideal for polling loops.
